title: Root-normalized identification of the two finite positive twist presentations
statement: Fix the finite-coefficient setting [def-pur-conventions], the actual integral-reduced signed lines [def-pur-finite-tensor-reduction-data] and their normalized reduction maps [def-pur-finite-signed-reduction-comparisons]. Use the positive charts of [def-pur-finite-positive-root-charts] and the published shifted root charts [def-pur-finite-reduction-root-charts]. The canonical identification of the published shifted positive twist with the shifted degree-zero integral-reduced positive line is the unique isomorphism agreeing with these charts for every primitive root, including the zero stage. Define its coefficient reduction by the actual line reduction and scalar shift conjugated by these uniquely specified presentations.

proof.text: Since the exponent is a unit in the algebraically closed base field, obtain a primitive root zeta. Form the explicit ratio of its published shifted root chart (including the coefficient-unit comparison) and the inverse shifted integral-reduced positive chart.

For any other primitive root eta, write zeta=eta^a by the cyclicity theorem for roots of unity. Apply the two chart power laws: both homomorphisms change by the same natural-number scalar a^d. Shift and postcomposition with the fixed coefficient-unit chart preserve this scalar. Cancel the eta positive chart and use bilinearity of composition to show that the two ratios agree. Convert the equality to the required heterogeneous equality.

Any comparison satisfying every chart equation agrees with the constructed ratio on the chosen root zeta, proving uniqueness. The existing canonical positive presentation and reduction definitions then use this unchanged existence-and-uniqueness theorem.
